preamble: In Rendille, a Somaloid language of northern Kenya, the Proto-East Cushitic consonant reconstructed as *z became the palatal glide /j/, where Somali, Afar and Oromo have the stop /d/. Ehret notes that the phonetic value of Proto-Cushitic *z is unknown and proposes a voiced palatal stop [ɟ], which would make the glide a lenition of a palatal; Beja shows the same glide reflex after vowels in Ehret's sound-change sequence.

examples.note: Sasse's correspondence table lists Rendille /j/ for Proto-East Cushitic *z against /d/ in Somali, Saho–Afar and Oromo.

languageExamples.language: Proto-Oti-Volta to Core Eastern Oti-Volta (Nateni, Mbelime, Byali)

examples.to: Nateni yūūdí, Mbelime yūùdè, Byali ywōī
examples.note: Forms in Eddyshaw's transcription: j = [ɟ], y = [j], ɩ ʋ = [ɪ ʊ], a tilde below a vowel marks nasalization, ' marks a glottalized vowel; POV = Proto-Oti-Volta; the final syllable of nouns is a noun-class suffix. Western Oti-Volta keeps z (Kusaal zūgɔ́, Mooré zúgù).

examples.to: Byali yūúm, Nateni yòmū, Mbelime yùòmū
Nateni yùkū, Mbelime yūùhṵ̀, Byali ywōhṵ̄
examples.note: Eddyshaw: POV *z becomes y in Core Eastern Oti-Volta and j in Nawdm; Gurma has y before rounded vowels (Gulimancema yòmā 'flour', yùlī 'head') and s elsewhere.
